title: Glossary — Supply on Hand for the Bridge (Retail Pharmacy Network Benefit)
content:
**Supply on hand for the bridge.** For an emergency supply under the Retail Pharmacy Network Benefit, the supply on hand for the bridge is anchored on the fill the member actually holds of the drug under review:

1. when an approved paper claim for the drug has a date of service later than every paid network claim for it, the days not yet run out of that paper-claim fill are counted, an approved paper claim being a fill on its date of service;
2. when, with no such paper claim, the member's most recent paid network claim for the drug carries a reversal, nothing is counted, because that fill was never dispensed;
3. otherwise the days not yet run out of the most recent paid network claim are counted.

**Days not yet run out.** A fill's days supply less the calendar days from its date of service (day zero) to today, never below zero. For an approved paper claim, the fill is the one on the paper claim's date of service with the days supply recorded on the approval; where several approved paper claims exist for the drug, the one with the latest date of service is the one compared.

**Approved paper claim with no paid network claim.** Where the member has an approved paper claim for the drug and no paid network claim for it at all, the paper-claim fill is the one counted.

## Usage examples (hypothetical records; today is day 30)

| Records for the drug | Supply on hand |
|---|---|
| Paid network claim of 30 days dated day 0; approved paper claim of 30 days dated day 12 | Paper-claim fill: 30 less 18, that is 12 |
| Paid network claim of 30 days dated day 20, with a reversal; no approved paper claim | 0 |
| Paid network claim of 30 days dated day 20, no reversal | 30 less 10, that is 20 |
| Approved paper claim of 14 days dated day 25; no paid network claim | 14 less 5, that is 9 |
| Paid network claim of 30 days dated day 20; approved paper claim dated day 10 | The paper claim is not later, so 20 |
